Alex: Heads-up: we saw a sharp tail-latency spike on the EFA cluster during the nightly TPU-like load test, cc perf team.
perf-bot: ALERT perf/regression: 99.9th latency +4.8x vs baseline on job=train-bench-64 (efa-us-west2).
Marta: Any hints from profiling? nvlink vs pcie path?
Alex: Short summary: multi-GPU, TP + tensor parallel mix. All-reduce seems to be taking long pauses around step boundaries. GPU compute utilization stays ~70% but network busy time shows spikes.
Jia: Pasted the lightweight perf dump:
```
# netprobe summary (shortened)
node0 -> node1: 12.3 GB/s avg, bursts to 28 GB/s
nvlink local: 45% utilization
pcie tx queue depth: 98% saturation during tails
nccl allreduce time (4096B elems): mean 3.1ms, p99 76ms
```
Jia: Also saw frequent kernel fallback to generic matmul kernel at seq_len>=1536, likely due to autotuner change yesterday.
Sam: Could be two things: (1) kernel selection regressed -> more compute stalls waiting for comm, (2) KV cache warmup is triggering cross-node fetches at step boundaries and inflating all-reduce windows.
Alex: Agreed. Repro steps I ran: `./tools/run_bench --topo efa --nodes 4 --tp 2 --bs 8 --seq 1600 --iters 200`. Repro is consistent.
Marta: Can someone share the NCCL and runtime env we used? I want to try forcing algorithm fallback.
Jia: Env: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`, `NCCL_ALGO=ring`, `RUNTIME_KERNEL_TUNER=auto` (default). When I forced `NCCL_ALGO=tree` p99 dropped ~30% but mean unchanged.
Sam: Forcing `ring` vs `tree` giving different tails suggests topology-aware routing matters. EFA topology has intermittent cross-rack hops that are being chosen by the default algorithm.
Alex: I captured a short trace with timeline markers (attached to thread). Key things: all-reduce overlap window grows right after a KV cache miss spike.
Marta: Quick mitigation idea: 1) pin kernel selection to pre-regression profile on affected models, 2) add soft-delay to KV-prefetch to smooth cross-node bursts, 3) try NCCL topo heuristics override. Anyone up for trying 1 and 2?
Sam: I can try pinning kernel selection. Which config key?
Alex: `runtime.kernelselect.policy = "pinned:v2026-03-01"` in job config. On the bench, that drops the number of generic fallbacks by ~70%.
Jia: I ran the pre-regression pinned config: p99 improved, but still some spikes from cross-node KV fetches. Adding a tiny async prefetch jitter helped reduce simultaneous fetches in my run.
Marta: OK let's do this plan: Sam pins kernels and posts the exact job config; Jia runs jittered KV prefetch (try jitter 5-20ms) and posts perf diff; I'll run a net-only probe to map hot crosslinks (`./tools/netprobe --mode heatmap --duration 60 --topo efa`).
Alex: Thanks team. If we confirm improvement, we'll roll a hotfix: revert tuner change and add KV prefetch backpressure in runtime.
Marta: Filing a short follow-up ticket with steps, labels: perf/regression, hotfix, infra:efa. :white_check_mark:
__notes: follow-up artifacts: small attachments referenced (trace, netprobe heatmap).
